text:
jess: FYI - customer X saw duplicate provisional tokens after a resumed streaming session. looks like snapshot hysteresis + route fallback interacting badly. cc @nate

nate: ugh. any logs? which route did it fallback to? :thinking_face:

jess: grabbed logs, small snippet below. session resumed, snapshot TTL expired, we tried hysteresis merge and also routed to alt-pool. ledger recorded provisional tokens twice.

```
INFO 2026-03-22T14:00:00Z session_id=abc123 resume from snapshot=SNAP-42 ttl_expired=true route=pool-a fallback=pool-b provisional_tokens=48
INFO 2026-03-22T14:00:01Z ledger-write provisional session_id=abc123 tokens=48 origin=resume
INFO 2026-03-22T14:00:01Z ledger-write provisional session_id=abc123 tokens=48 origin=fallback
```

karen: interesting - so two distinct origins wrote provisional entries within 1s. hysteresis logic was supposed to dedupe if same session_id within window. maybe session_id namespace collision between pool-a and pool-b?

sam: we have a known quirk where resume HMAC key differs per pool leading to slightly different derived session ids (we canonicalize later). that could bypass dedupe.

nate: timeline: resume triggers snapshot merge (hysteresis checks), then route policy decides fallback mid-merge -> two independent code paths call ledger.write without dedupe check. sounds like an ordering/race.

jess: customer impact: small token bump but shows up on console as two provisional charges. ops flagged it as duplicate and manually refunded. want to prevent recurrence and improve console signal.

karen: short term: add an idempotency check in ledger.write for provisional entries keyed by canonical_session_id + origin_hint; if canonicalization missing, fall back to best-effort HMAC. also add telemetry tag to easily find collisions.

sam: agree. we should also make routing policy pause until snapshot merge finishes or use a single merge RPC that performs canonicalization inside the merge to avoid two writes.

nate: for observability: add a console flag that surfaces "resume-hysteresis-collision" events on the session timeline and a counts card on the model/route dashboard. ops wants to see count + last-seen + example session_id.

jess: UX ask: when a provisional charge is later deduped/refunded, can we show that in the cost waterfall? right now it looks like two charges, then a refund ticket - messy.

karen: doable. console change: annotate provisional charges with "provisional_id" and link refunds to original provisional_id so waterfall can collapse them. low-risk and helps customer support.

sam: also propose a rollout: patch ledger.write with idempotency + telemetry behind a kill-switch, deploy to canary pools for 48h, then flip for all. add a migration job to retroactively canonicalize recent provisional dupes for last 7 days.

nate: migration needs care - avoid rewriting settled confirmed charges. only affect provisional entries not confirmed and not older than 7d. ops-bot: schedule?

ops-bot: migration job queued: "merge-provisional-hysteresis-collisions-v1" targeting provisional entries from 2026-03-15 to 2026-03-22. estimate ~12k rows. will run in dry-run mode first.

jess: perfect. can we also tag metric: "provisional.dedupe.miss.count" and a trace span in merge path? want to bake into rollout dashboard.

karen: yes. I'll add the metric + a dashboard row showing pre/post canary rates. also add an alert if dedupe miss > 1% sustained over 30m.

sam: dev note: watch out for per-pool HMAC secret rotation. canonicalization must read secrets consistently. if we canonicalize using per-tenant master key, that avoids pool divergence.

nate: thanks all. action items: karen PR for ledger idempotency + metric; sam PR for single-merge RPC; jess coordinate console annotation + support docs; ops-bot run dry-run migration and report. plan to roll canary in 48h.

jess: I'll open threads for each. low-severity but visible to customers so prioritize. :thumbsup:
